I'll start by reading the guide and the package layout.

Some reads failed with transient errors. I'll retry them.

Now rewriting the command modules, starting with `listing.py`.

No git is available and I've overwritten the originals. I'll rebuild them from what I read earlier into `/tmp/orig`, then run a differential fuzz against the refactor.

Now I'll write the original command modules back into the copy.

The refactored package matched the original on all 28,800 randomized runs, and the outcomes covered every exit status. Next I'll add `tests/test_access.py`.

That failure is a bug in my test: it reused the loop's last grant, whose granter is `nobody`. I'll fix the test.

The refactor is done and `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

I added `docshelf/access.py` with the public names from the guide, and every access check now goes through it. Each of `listing`, `show`, `edit`, `share`, `delete` and `audit` has a module-level `RULES` that passes to each call into `access`. `store.py`, `render.py` and `errors.py` are untouched, and the public functions of the other modules keep their names and parameters.

**Checks**
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` passed all 30 tests, exit code 0, including my new `tests/test_access.py`. The existing tests are unchanged.
- No git was available and I had already overwritten the originals. So I rebuilt the original command modules in `/tmp/orig` from what I had read. I then ran random workspaces and commands (28,800 runs across 3 seeds) through both versions. Stdout, stderr, exit status and every workspace file, including `activity.log`, were identical, and the runs covered exit statuses 0, 2, 3 and 4. The rebuilt originals are my own copy, so the fuzz is only as good as that copy.
- A grep outside `access.py`, `store.py`, `render.py` and `errors.py` finds no decision on role, status, grants, delegations, `granted_by`, owner, team or level. The only remaining matches are fields printed in output and the `status=3` keyword argument in `show`.

**Rules per command**

| Command | roles | suspension | ends | delegation | blank team | `*` grant needs admin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list`, `show` | folded | through | exclusive | all | no for `list`, yes for `show` | yes |
| `audit` | folded | through | exclusive | none | no | yes |
| `edit` | lower | before | inclusive | owned | no | no |
| `share`, `delete` | exact | status | exclusive | none | no | no |

**Quirks kept as they were**
- `edit` ends grants and delegations at the `until` minute inclusive; the other commands end them before it.
- `edit` lets a suspension end when the `until` day starts, readers the day after, and `share` and `delete` refuse any suspended account.
- `show` treats users with no team as members of `team` documents with no team. `list` and `audit` do not, and neither does `edit`.
- `edit` accepts any `*` grant. The readers accept one only when an admin granted it.
- A delegate can edit with what the lender owns or was granted, but not with the lender's role or team. `share` and `delete` ignore delegations.

I also kept the `store.users[user_id]` lookups so a direct call with an unknown user still raises `KeyError` as before.

cd /app/docshelf && cat store.py errors.py render.py __init__.py __main__.py cli.py; cat ../docs/changelog.md
cd /app/docshelf && cat listing.py show.py edit.py share.py delete.py audit.py
cd /app/docshelf && cat share.py; echo ======; cat audit.py
cd /app && git status --short 2>&1 | head; git log --oneline 2>&1 | head -3

cd /app && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -15
